nodes.label: claude-sonnet-5 offline arm
nodes.rationale: Named claude-sonnet-5 -- a REAL arm name -- on purpose, because model_name doubles as the PRICE_BOOK key: a name like mock-ok raises UnknownModelError inside cost_usd, assemble_record catches it, and the record's turns/tokens/cost are all zero with only trajectory_parse_error set, so the offline gate would be measuring the price book rather than the topology. api_base carries neither /v1/messages nor a trailing /v1 because LiteLLM's anthropic provider appends it, exactly as the mantle Sonnet arm does.

nodes.label: gemma-4-31b offline arm (sampling probe)
nodes.rationale: Exists to carry sampling. Section 5.3 puts sampling entirely in proxy config because Claude Code has no temperature flag, and Task 11 could not tell whether a deployment-level temperature survives to the wire -- it was absent from optional_params, litellm_params and standard_logging_object on the mock path, which short-circuits before provider param transformation. A real provider call answers the question, and this arm asks it for free. Values match the production gemma arm so the answer transfers.

nodes.label: kimi-k2-5 offline arm (tool-id patch detector)
nodes.rationale: The only offline arm that reaches the openai->anthropic adapter. The two anthropic/ arms bypass it entirely, so the 2026-08-07 tool-id defect -- LiteLLM rewriting Kimi's `functions.Read:0` to `functions_Read_0` and breaking its tool loop -- was structurally invisible to this gate and cost a live run to find. The stub answers with a Kimi-shaped tool_call id and REJECTS a tool_call_id it never issued, so if bakeoff.litellm_patches stops applying the id comes back mangled, the stub 400s, and this arm goes red -- the only way the gate can tell a live patch from a dead one. Carries additional_drop_params per deployment because the global litellm_settings entry measurably does NOT reach an openai/ deployment's param validation.

nodes.label: fixtures/anthropic_stub.py streaming endpoint
nodes.rationale: A real streaming Anthropic endpoint rather than a mock_response deployment, and that distinction is the whole reason litellm_smoke_offline.yaml exists. It also serves /v1/chat/completions with a Kimi-shaped tool_call id and rejects ids it never issued, which is what makes the tool-id patch detectable offline.

nodes.label: mock_response short-circuits the streaming callback
nodes.rationale: LiteLLM's mock short-circuits inside anthropic_messages before the provider call, so a STREAMING request never reaches the streaming wrapper that fires the success callback on stream completion. Measured against litellm 1.95.0 with claude 2.1.220: two calls made, only the non-streaming one captured. Every real Claude Code call is streaming, so a gate built on mocks would certify capture that does not happen -- the same class of defect as Task 11's defect 15.

nodes.label: Offline gate must mirror production settings
nodes.rationale: use_chat_completions_url_for_anthropic_messages, additional_drop_params and num_retries are mirrored from litellm_config.yaml, because a setting that differs between the two files is a section 5.2 divergence in the gate itself -- the offline gate would exercise different routing than the run it is meant to certify.
